title: B1142 HVAC Repair; Out of Scope Roof Modification
description: This document approves the award of a modification to a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Task Order (TO) Under contract FA251720D0004 under the Front Range Multiple Award Construction Contract (FRMACC) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ). The current TO FA251725F0154 is to provide HVAC work at Building 1142 (Project TDKA 10-1128). The intended action is to modify the current TO and include roof and lighting work for B1142. The justification is to award a modification to aforementioned on-going TO as it is in the interest of efficiency and economy. It is economically sound due to heavy equipment rentals/laborers/etc. that are already scheduled to be on site, alleviating additional mobilization and demobilization costs for a potentially different contractor if competed and awarded other than sole-source. This new requirement for roof replacement, lighting replacement, and interior finishes repair directly overlaps with ongoing work in the facility being performed by the current contractor. The Contractor is familiar with the facility, is in direct control of the construction schedule of HVAC replacement scope already awarded, and can execute the additional scope identified at a lower cost and shorter timeframe than other FRMACC contractors due to the efficiency of de-conflicting overlapping scopes. Positive impacts include assurance of proper sequencing of integrated work to avoid duplication of efforts and costs, elimination of warranty conflicts between contracts, and reduction of mission impact to execute consolidated scope in tandem in lieu of extended, multiple efforts displacing the mission owner on multiple occasions. Examples of overlapping scope with potential for duplicated costs and time include rooftop unit and associated curb placement/detailing on roof, roof-mounted utilities impacted by roof replacement, lighting and interior HVAC rework in tandem with ceiling replacement. Additionally, the roof conditions of this facility are in severe need of repair to mitigate ongoing mission impact in the facility, and are essential to be executed with urgency and without delay related to current awarded HVAC replacement work. This modification was executed by the 21st Contracting Squadron, located at 135 Dover St, Bldg 350, Suite 2225, Peterson Space Force Base, CO 80914. Olgoonik Enterprises, LLC (CAGE: 819A4) received the awarded modification for new work in the amount of $1,355,810.00. The modification was executed on 09/25/2026. Please submit all questions/concerns to the Contracting Officer at frederick.chartrand@spaceforce.mil.

description: Note: A Market Survey to Assess Small Business Capability was posted for this procurement on 05 March 2025 under E-Commerce control number MKTSVY-0019F306, REFERENCE NUMBER: N6600125R0025. The Naval Information Warfare Center (NIWC) Pacific intends to issue Request for Proposal (RFP) No. N6600126R0019 for Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) Systems and Information Operations (IO) from Seabed to Space (S2ISR). The services contemplated under this effort will provide the Navy with the ability to develop and field ISR systems that incorporate the latest capabilities for maintaining robust communication, surveillance, and security to accommodate advances in technology and other complementary systems while countering ever-increasing threats. The Government contemplates that, in its capacity, the contractor will provide technical support services in the form of algorithm development, data design processing, hardware and software development, fabrication, installation, testing, deployment, recovery, repair, systems engineering, program and configuration management, logistics, maintenance, sustainment, training, environmental support, and analysis in support of ISR activities, ISR systems, and corresponding cybersecurity operations. ISR activities may include support related to chemical, nuclear, biological, and radiological (CNBR) elements related to unmanned system. ISR systems may include surveillance programs, systems, networks, and tactical data communications systems including automated radio communications systems, satellite terminal systems, and space, air, land and water autonomous or non-autonomous systems that could be used in ISR operations. Contract activities may be performed throughout the world. In addition, work may be performed onboard afloat vessels (including U.S. Coast Guard vessels), in port, or at sea alongside coalition partner nations (e.g., NATO countries). It is anticipated that the procurement will result in the award of multiple indefinite-delivery, indefinite quantity (IDIQ) contracts with cost-plus-fixed-fee (CPFF) and cost (no fee) pricing arrangements. The period of performance will include a seven-year ordering period. Orders will be placed pursuant to the ordering processes of FAR 16.505(a). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 541715 Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering and Life Sciences, excluding nanotechnology and biotechnology and the Small Business Size Standard is 1,000. Security classification will vary from Unclassified to Top Secret/Incidental Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) classification. This requirement will be competed on a full-and-open basis. This is a follow-on requirement covered by contracts N6600121D0053 through 0063. NIWC Pacific anticipates that the final RFP for N6600126R0019 will be released no earlier than 21 November 2025. The solicitation will be available electronically via the Solicitation Module within the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) website at https://piee.eb.mil, under Notice ID N6600126R0019.

Sterile Processing Departments (SPD) are the backbone surgical instrument sterilization for MTFs. When SPDs are unusable because of onsite equipment failure, operating room and clinic procedures decrease by greater than 90%, essentially halting the surgical capability of the MTFs. The cessation of surgical cases results in decreased provider readiness, risk of Graduate Medical Education (GME) citation, and severely impacted healthcare delivery. title: ATR Loop Pressurizer Fabrication
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from qualified vendors capable of fabricating an ASME Section VIII, Division 2 pressure vessel for use as the ATR Loop Pressurizer (1A-NE Loop). The fabricated vessel will play a critical role in maintaining system pressure, degassing, and surge compensation for an Advanced Test Reactor (ATR) experiment loop. BACKGROUND INL is a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratory dedicated to nuclear energy, national security, and clean energy innovation. The ATR experiment loops rely on a dynamic pressurizer system to maintain primary coolant pump pressure, provide a means of degassing the primary coolant, and compensate for pressure surges. BEA is requesting vendor capability statements for the fabrication of a vertically oriented, leg-mounted pressure vessel with radial side arms, built to strict nuclear, metallurgical, and structural performance standards. Project-specific INL drawings, design calculations, and procedural references will be furnished to selected vendors. The scope of work includes the following: Fabrication, inspection, and physical testing of one (1) ASME Section VIII, Division 2 stainless steel pressure vessel with associated appurtenances (vessel, mounting leg stand, spray nozzles, lifting lugs), per INL Drawings 1050604, 1050605, and 1050606 Supply of all materials associated with the vessel and appurtenances Hydrostatic testing at room temperature in accordance with ASME code (minimum test pressure 3415 psig, +100/-0 psig tolerance) Load testing and documentation of lifting lugs Shop drawing development and submission through INL's vendor data system Shipping/handling pallet and container for horizontal-orientation transport, forklift-compatible Delivery to WestOne Logistics, Idaho Falls, ID The scope of work does not include the following: Installation at the Contractor's facility Procurement and installation of clamp-on heaters Vessel insulation Design, seismic analysis, thermal analysis, stress analysis, or fatigue analysis Overpressure protection (provided by a separate direct spring relief valve) Floor mounting plate APPLICABLE CODES AND REFERENCES The fabrication and associated documentation must comply with the following (as applicable to component type): ASME Section VIII, Division 2 (2025) AISC 370 (2021) ANSI/AISC N690-18 (Nuclear Facility Steel Structures) ASCE 4-16 and ASCE 43-19 (Seismic Design) ASME NQA-1 (2022 edition) DESIGN REQUIREMENTS Vendors should have demonstrated experience with nuclear-grade pressure vessel fabrication and must meet or exceed the following design conditions: Materials & Components: Vessel and lifting lugs: Type 347 stainless steel Mounting legs: Type 316 stainless steel Vertically oriented, leg-mounted vessel with elliptical heads and four (4) radially arranged side arms Pressure & Temperature Ratings: Vessel Internal Design Pressure: 2500 psig Vessel Design Temperature: 668�F Normal Operating Pressure: 300�2208 psig; Normal Operating Temperature: 422�650�F Heater Leg Design Pressure: 2500 psig; Heater Leg Design Temperature: 800�F Vessel designed to Section VIII with seismic input per ASCE 4 and ASCE 43 (stand per AISC 370/N690) Fluid Service: High-purity, radioactive, demineralized water; pH range 5.0�11.0 Dissolved solids ?10 ppm, suspended matter ?3 ppm, chlorides ?0.5 ppm, dissolved gas ?150 cc/kg Cyclic Service: Pressurizer cycled between ambient and normal operating pressure 18 times/year over a 60-year design life (1,080 total cycles) Inspections & Engineering Approval: All pressure boundary welds (butt welds, with limited exceptions) inspected per ASME VIII/NDE requirements, including full volumetric inspection of all four side-arm weld joints Fabrication drawings and calculations submitted for formal BEA review/approval through the vendor data system PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested vendors should submit an Expression of Interest that includes the following: Company name and point of contact Relevant fabrication experience, particularly nuclear or DOE-grade ASME Section VIII pressure vessel work Applicable NAICS codes and business size classification Any existing DOE or federal contracting experience (if applicable) Demonstrated capability to meet ASME, AISC, and seismic-informed design requirements Acknowledgment of the ability to meet the following vendor data submittals: Shop drawings and bill of materials Certified Material Test Reports (CMTRs) for weld filler material, spray nozzles, steel shapes/plates/piping Welding procedure specifications (WPS) and welder qualification/continuity logs NDE procedures, personnel qualifications, and inspection reports Lifting lug load test report Cleaning procedure and cleanliness report Internal/external surface finish reports Hydrostatic test procedure and report ASME U-1A Data Report As-built drawings Completed Vendor Data Schedule and transmittal forms (Form 431.13/431.14) QUALITY ASSURANCE REQUIREMENTS The subcontractor's quality program must be equivalent to ASME NQA-1 (2022 edition). Requirements include: Qualification records for welders, inspectors, and NDE technicians (including eye exams) Third-party inspection where required M&TE calibration records Certificates of Conformance (CoC) and ASME Pressure Vessel certification Submittal of all quality-related inspection and test documents FABRICATION & TESTING Materials must meet applicable ASME and ASTM specifications; Commercial Use (QL3) quality level per NQA-1 All pressure boundary joints are butt welds (limited fillet/stake weld exceptions for heater supports, trunnion plate, and spray nozzle attachment) Welds ground and polished flush prior to NDE Internal surfaces: 250 microinch Ra or better (except nozzles); heater leg exterior: 125 microinch Ra or better Cleaning to Class B cleanliness per ASME Code, both prior to final assembly and via final flush No paint on internal or external surfaces Hydrostatic testing per ASME Section VIII, Division 2 requirements BEA inspectors may witness fabrication and testing activities, withhold points specified at least 2 weeks in advance ASME "U" stamp certification of the vessel DELIVERY & PROTECTION Final vessel must be delivered to WestOne Logistics, 1765 North Yellowstone Highway, Idaho Falls, ID 83401, with: Vessel fully flushed, drained, and dried with no residual moisture prior to packaging Packed and shipped in horizontal orientation with suitable protective fixtures/fittings Clear labeling of purchase order number, gross weight, and lifting points Unit prepared for forklift handling; lifting diagram provided prior to shipment All shipping documents included in a waterproof envelope INL personnel retain rights for inspections, audits, and hold-point reviews throughout fabrication. Final acceptance occurs at the Subcontractor's facility prior to shipment and again upon arrival at WestOne Logistics. Deadline for submission: November 6, 2026 Submit to: Chase.egbert@inl.gov Only select respondents, as determined by BEA, will receive an invitation to participate in the anticipated RFP solicitation. title: Request for Information (RFI) Obtaining Food Franchise Rights in Washington, DC - National Capital Region (NCR)
description: Request for Information (RFI) : Obtaining Food Franchise Rights in Washington, DC - Northern Capital Region (NCR) The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to gather detailed input from qualified organizations regarding the requirements, processes, and opportunities associated with obtaining food franchise rights within the Northern Capital Region (NCR), Washington, DC. Organizations responding to this RFI are requested to provide all relevant documentation, points of contact, marketing materials, and procedural information. This RFI is for planning and informational purposes only and does not obligate the Government to pursue any further action or future solicitation. Direct Engagement Model � Industry Feedback Requested In addition to information on obtaining food franchise rights generally, the FBI is specifically interested in understanding the feasibility and attractiveness of a direct-engagement model, in which the FBI would contract or otherwise arrange directly with individual food franchise brands (rather than through a single master food-service contractor) to provide food service operations within the J. Edgar Hoover Building (JEH), Washington, DC. What the FBI should understand about this model: Typical franchise agreement structures, term lengths, and capital investment requirements (buildout, equipment, branding) when a franchisor/franchisee operates within a federal government-controlled facility rather than a traditional commercial or retail location Licensing, royalty, and territory considerations that may apply or require modification for a single-tenant government building Food safety, supply chain, and operational standards the franchise would need to meet or adapt to operate within a secure federal facility Any precedent for franchise operations within federal buildings, military installations, or other access-controlled environments, and lessons learned from those arrangements All responses must be submitted to: Ms. McKenzie P. Bucher, mpbucher@fbi.gov Mr. Tom Teets, twteets@fbi.gov Please provide all requested information no later than September 21, 2026, at 12:00 PM EDT.

description: NASA/KSC has a requirement for continued operation and expansion of the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex (KSCVC) Public Visitor Program (PVP) to include the creation and operation of a new Astronaut Training Experience (ATX) facility for guests. The KSCVC serves as a critical national asset that reaches more than 1.6 million visitors annually and communicates NASA�s mission to the public. Through its PVP, the KSCVC ignites support for NASA initiatives by engaging the public in NASA�s robust history, dynamic present, and inspirational future. Public demand for the current ATX facility greatly outnumbers current operational capacity and reimagined content is vital to communicate NASA�s mission, maintain public enthusiasm, and reinforce support for major programs. A new public ATX will increase capacity; introduce learners to career technical skills desired by the administration and industry; provide a high-tech environment with labs, workshops and makerspaces; and meet the increasing demand of public visitors nationwide. Because these activities are expected to extend beyond the expiration date of the current KSCVC agreement, continuity of performance is necessary to ensure successful project execution and operations at a reasonable profit. Transitioning responsibility to a successor concessionaire during the design, construction, or commissioning phases significantly increase performance, schedule, and integration risk, adversely impacting NASA/KSC�s objectives for timely delivery and operation of the new ATX facility.
